採用・広告の製品.quote: Q5D’s wiring automation robots are changing the way vehicles are built. Cost savings from 10X productivity gains are matched by sensational improvements in electrical/electronic functionality and wiring quality and consistency.

Following early engagements in the automotive sector, Q5D has attracted customers in the aerospace and defence, and consumer electrical goods sectors. As the need for electrification spreads to products in many more industries, the company’s technology will be applicable to these too.

Q5D’s 5-axis robots address one of the most persistent bottlenecks in modern manufacturing: the manual assembly of wiring harnesses. Still done by hand in industries like automotive, aerospace, and consumer electronics, this labour-intensive process is costly, error-prone, and frequently offshored to low-wage countries.

Our wiring automation removes the need for wiring harness inventory and unlocks substantial improvements in wiring efficiency, weight, and reliability. For example, in the automotive sector, conservative estimates suggest that this automation can reduce wiring costs by up to 200 USD per compact vehicle.
A complete production package

Q5D’s customer Technical Assessment Centre (TAC) at its Portishead, Bristol, UK, facility is designed to help customers with feasibility studies, design for manufacturing, and prototyping as they transition from traditional wire harnesses to full automation.

The company targets manufacturers needing complex wiring systems, offering hardware-as-a-service with design/production software, digital twins, and bespoke support to onshore production and support just-in-time orders.[2] Growth momentum stems from its world-first automation approach, demonstrated impact across applications, and active status with recent accounts filed through 2024.[1][4]

Pivotal moments include launching hardware that integrates electrical functions using 5-axis robots, simplifying supply chains, and gaining visibility in sectors hungry for productivity gains, as evidenced by its ongoing operations and recent financial filings.[1][4]
: CY10 and SQ25 machines paired with CAD/CAM design tools, digital twins, and production software for seamless workflow from design to on-demand manufacturing.[2]
: Delivers error reduction, supply chain simplification (co-located production eliminates inventory/logistics costs), weight/space savings, and design freedom—key for automotive and aerospace.[2]

: Hardware-as-a-service model with bespoke support, high-speed large-format production (SQ25), and applicability across consumer/industrial sectors, outperforming manual methods in accuracy and JIT responsiveness.[1][2]
